title: Local actions and territorial land disputes
shortTitle: Local actions and territorial land disputes
summary: The historical local-action rule associated certain claims involving land with courts where the land was located. The readings examine the rule’s origins, contested rationale, and later statutory treatment.
notes: The cases arise in different jurisdictions and periods. Do not treat the older local-action doctrine as the unqualified modern federal venue rule.

sections.Meaning: The historical local-action rule associated certain claims involving land with courts where the land was located. The readings examine the rule’s origins, contested rationale, and later statutory treatment.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify whether the action determines title or possession or instead seeks personal damages, and distinguish subject-matter authority from venue. Compare Livingston’s historical restriction with Reasor-Hill’s rejection of denying a remedy solely on that basis.
